summary: The appeals challenged the Calcutta High Court's 2008 decision allowing specific performance of a contract dated 29.03.1999 between the plaintiff (respondent) and defendant no.1, setting aside the trial court's dismissal. Key issues included the validity and enforceability of the agreement to sell, alleged coercion in its execution, maintainability, limitation, part performance under Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, and whether appellants (defendant nos.2 and 3) were bona fide purchasers for value. The Supreme Court examined evidence of advance payment, possession, development activities, and conflicting claims of coercion and prior agreement in favor of the appellants. The trial court had dismissed the suit, but the High Court reversed, decreeing specific performance.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act
Section 36 of the Indian Stamp Act
Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act
Section 144(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
final_judgment: Appeals allowed; High Court judgment set aside; trial court's dismissal of the suit restored; suit for specific performance dismissed.
